classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that both triangles share the parallelogram's base length and perpendicular height, add their half-products, then calculate directly using the explicitly requested parallelogram formula.

content.prompt: Treat this parallelogram as two triangles. Calculate the area of the parallelogram by:

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9, shared diagram to the right of part a
spec.description: Unfilled parallelogram with horizontal bases, sides sloping down to the right, a dashed upper-left to lower-right diagonal, single parallel arrows on the bases and double parallel arrows on the sloping sides. The perpendicular height is shown externally on the left.
spec.mathematics: Both triangles have base 6.7 mm and perpendicular height 4.2 mm. The diagonal partitions the parallelogram into two equal-area triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry, dimensions and parallel markers are permanent student givens; no calculated areas appear.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Adding the areas of the triangles.

answer.worked:
Each triangle has base $6.7\,\text{mm}$ and perpendicular height $4.2\,\text{mm}$.
$$\begin{align*}A &= \left(\frac{1}{2}\times4.2\times6.7\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2}\times4.2\times6.7\right)\\A &= 14.07+14.07\\A &= 28.14\,\text{mm}^2\end{align*}$$
